name: Huchiun-Aguasto Ohlone village at Tormey (Rodeo) - the 400-500 of 1776
shape_note: Domed/conical tule-thatched family house on a bent-willow pole frame, about 3-5 m across (as in early_sf.csv; Milliken 2009 ch.3). Count is an ESTIMATE at ~6-8 people per house. Anza's party camped at Rodeo Creek on 1 Apr 1776 and next morning passed through a village of 'some four hundred persons' (Font) / 'about five hundred souls' (Anza) 'in a little valley on the bank of a small arroyo', less than a quarter league east of camp; Bolton identifies it 'at Tormey'. The largest Bay Area village reported by the Spaniards (also Canizares 1775); Milliken suspects a seasonal gathering place. Local tribe Huchiun-Aguasto (San Francisco Bay Costanoan); they moved to Mission Dolores 1803-1810, the last with the Carquins in Jun 1809 - Feb 1810 (Milliken 2009 ch.5). SUPERSEDES early_region hch_aguasto_village (same village, placed by guess near Pinole Creek with end 1800). Position precision ~1 km (Bolton's identification of Font's/Anza's village).
